description: Solo developer from Ribeirão Preto (Brazil) building Earthset, a 3D game where players run a base at the Moon's south pole. Lighting, Earth communication and storms come from real NASA data. Three ranks adapt the game for ages 8 to adults. Looking for teammates with 3D modeling or pixel art skills, UX and educational content writers, and anyone with a space science or data background to check the scientific accuracy.
summary: Earthset is a browser-based 3D base-management game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players run a small base at the Moon's south pole through one 708-hour lunar day. They manage solar power, which the terrain blocks for long stretches, plus water, air and food, while two astronauts and a rover carry out tasks. A greenhouse grows food, and LUMA, a rule-based guide, explains what is at risk. The player wins by reaching hour 708 with at least one heart left, and loses when all three are gone. The sun path, lunar horizon and space-weather events come from NASA/JPL Horizons, LRO LOLA and NASA DONKI, and illustrative parts are labelled on screen. The game runs in English and Brazilian Portuguese and includes a school mode. It makes survival trade-offs visible and teaches how real lunar data shapes a mission. The project has 598 automated tests, but it has not yet been tested with new players.
details:
Project details

Earthset is a browser-based 3D base-management game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players run a small crewed base at the Moon's south pole through one 708-hour lunar day. Solar power is available only when the Sun is above the measured local horizon, and terrain blocks it for long stretches. Players balance power, water, air and food. Two astronauts inspect, harvest and maintain the base, and shelter during solar radiation events. A rover makes ice trips for water, installs solar panels and repairs the antenna. A greenhouse produces food, and its wear reduces yield over time. The player wins by reaching hour 708 with at least one heart left, and loses when all three hearts are gone. A heart is lost after six hours with a vital resource at zero.

Benefits and intended impact

Earthset makes the trade-offs of lunar survival visible and playable. It requires no installation and runs in any modern browser, including on phones. It is available in English and Brazilian Portuguese and includes a school mode with plain-language labels for classroom use. The intended audience is students and educators interested in space exploration. The project is at an early stage: it has not yet been tested with students or new players.
